findings.reason: the extra tests still have to pass and cost a node nothing, and no implementer would follow them to the wrong mechanism; naming them is redundant rather than misleading.
findings.text: two of the four "existing settle tests" §10 requires to pass, `tests/test_follow_settled_rows.py` and `tests/test_follower_settles_a_promoted_row.py`, carry the pane's row settle and the ledger-row fold, not the drain-settle rule `_check_settle` (neither mentions `_check_settle`, `_population_has_live_work`, the settle interval or the grace variable), so they measure §8's row path rather than §10's move

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every symbol §10 cites resolves: `resumption.sweep`'s resume pass (`reckon/crew/resumption.py:1768-1795`), `sweep_unfollowed_sessions`'s host rule (`reckon/crew/runs.py:3746-3772`), `review_settle_seconds_remaining` reading `auto_resume` alone (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:1266`), `_latest_resume_at` returning the newer of the two stamps (`:206-222`), `resume_superseded_head` (`:78`), `_check_settle`/`saw_live`/`settle_populations` (`reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:1494-1560`), `_population_has_live_work` (`:482-506`), the grace and sample constants (`:285`, `:312`), and all four named test files; extensionless hrefs (`/reckon/research/monitor-storage-load-rca`, `/reckon/plans/the-monitor-shows-the-work-it-watches`, `/reckon/evidence/archive/the-monitor-reads-each-fact-once-landed`) each resolve once `.html` is appended.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the changed done-when is measurable and declares a control for each rule it keeps (populations, grace, `saw_live`, ownerless, unscoped), but two of the four "existing settle tests" it names do not exercise the drain-settle rule §10 changes.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §10 places no evidence in a scratch or node-local temporary path; its gates are named test files plus a 60 s `strace` whose log the node records on its own run record, and the plan names no transient location for it.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §10 names only code symbols and section numbers; no ticket number, version tag or changelog prose reaches a symbol, and the added prose states the mechanism (which decision rule is kept, which reading moves) rather than what changed.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — on the changed unit all three checks hold: the kept-rule description matches `_check_settle` line for line (populations from `settle_populations`, the 120 s grace from `_settle_grace_default`, the `if not saw_live: return` refusal, the `any()` hold and the `settle_empty_since` grace measure); swapping the directory listing inside `_population_has_live_work` is the one place `_is_live` reads from, so the mechanism produces the asserted measure; and the callers are named and real — the follower's wait pass (`crew_follow_commands.py:1759`, reached from the settle-aware `follow` at `:3035`) and the reflex's gate (`recovery_review_acceptance.py:462`, which returns `settling` while `remaining > 0`), the station loop being §7's.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §10 carries one goal, moving the reflex and settle detection to a single station-side execution, with the subscriber retaining its rule and changing only its reading source.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` declares `s10: [s7, s8]`, both of which §10 needs (the station loop §7 and the subscriber §8 that §10's 60 s trace measures), and `s12` depends on `s10`; no relationship points at a node that does not exist.
